Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

analysis noun

also analyse, analyze, analytical

classical

Cic. Div. 2.129: explicātiōne nātūrae
Cic. Fin. 3.14

explicātiō, explicātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

an analysis, a detailed account of a matter

An unfolding: Cicero’s word for setting out a subject point by point (Lewis & Short). To analyse, explicāre.

Other words

  • partītiō, partītiōnis f. — a division into parts, a logical analysis

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Top. 28: cum rēs ea, quae prōposita est, quasi in membra discerpitur (Lewis & Short)

  • ēnōdātiō, ēnōdātiōnis f. — an untangling, an explanation

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. ND 3.62: explicātiō fābulārum et ēnōdātiō nōminum; Cic. Top. 31 (Lewis & Short)

  • analysis, analysis f. — mathematical analysis

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. analysis, after Gauss

    Only of the branch of mathematics.

Examples

  • Utrum philosophiā dignius, sāgārum superstitiōne ista interpretārī an explicātiōne nātūrae?

    Which is worthier of philosophy: to interpret such things by the superstition of fortune-tellers, or by an analysis of nature?Cic. Div. 2.129

  • multumque ad ea, quae quaerimus, explicātiō tua ista prōfēcerit

    and that analysis of yours will help a great deal towards what we are looking forCic. Fin. 3.14

See also explain, research, detail.

SourcesLewis & Short: explicatio · Lewis & Short: partitio · Lewis & Short: enodatio

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. analysis.
